text:
morgan: anyone else seeing intermittent 502s for model-proxy in apac/eu since ~08:30? customer A reported TLS errors.
jin: seeing spikes in 502 and a bunch of TLS handshake failures in alb logs. looks like ALB is returning the default cert for some connections.
emily: ugh. that usually means SNI was missing/stripped and ALB fell back to default listener cert. any frontend proxies in the path?
morgan: ops-bot rolled ingress-v2 at 08:20 (canary to prod). @ops-bot posted deploy. might be related.
ops-bot: deploy ingress-v2 to prod complete — rollout started 2025-11-10T08:20:12Z, 35/35 pods ready.
jin: pulled a sample TCP dump from a failing client (apac). note the ClientHello has empty server_name.
jin: ```
14:02:13.123456 IP client->alb  TLS ClientHello
    extensions: server_name: (none)
    alpn: h2
```
liam: looks like our TCP sidecar (tls-proxy) was updated to do TLS passthrough -> then re-encrypt, but IIRC older passthrough builds stripped SNI when doing renegotiation.
emily: can you dump sidecar config? maybe we accidentally enabled TLS inspect at the WAF or set ALPN override.
jin: sidecar args on ingress: `--tls-passthrough=true --inspect=false --sni-preserve=false` — oh. that `sni-preserve=false` came from the rollout.
alex: whoops. that flag will strip SNI and re-initiate TLS, making ALB see no SNI -> default cert selected.
morgan: so why only apac/eu?
liam: some clients reuse TLS sessions / resume and others send SNI; also older client stacks omit SNI. mixed behavior + our sidecar change means only the ones that don't send SNI get default certs. regional variance due to client population.
emily: immediate mitigation: flip sni-preserve=true on sidecar, or force ALB to route using HTTP host header instead of SNI (terminate TLS at ALB). which is faster?
jin: quick rollback of the flag is fastest. I'll roll a patch to ingress-v2 canary and push to prod.
ops-bot: deployment ingress-v2-rollback started — stepping canary at 2025-11-10T09:02:45Z.
jin: rolled out sni-preserve=true across canary, monitoring.
emily: also capture a diff for listener rules — we should add a fallback rule that uses host header on the HTTP listener before relying on SNI for cert selection.
liam: good idea. ALB will pick default cert when SNI missing; host-header routing means TLS must be terminated at ALB (we currently do TLS passthrough for some services). need an RFC for which services require passthrough.
morgan: after rollback errors dropped to normal levels. thanks. can we add alerts for large fraction of connections presenting default cert?
alex: yes — CloudWatch metric `SSLNegotiationError` and we can parse `ssl_certificate` field in access logs to detect `CN=*.redwood-inference.net` as fallback.
emily: filing follow-up: add listener rule checklist (SNI reliance), add preflight for sidecar flags, and add metric/alert for default-cert rate. I'll own the follow-up.
morgan: thanks all :thumbsup: please add short postmortem once follow-ups are in.
alex: adding a note to infra runbook about sni-preserve default and canary guardrails.
jin: marking thread resolved for now, will post timeline in incidents channel if anything else pops up.
